main_text.l: Mediatoris nostri.Etsi vero Deus propter meritum Filii
sui peccata nobis remittit: nos tamen adhuc affligit
in hac vita, non quidem ut nos puniat sed ut nos pa-
terne castiget; & quia nos Deus non punit propter
peccata nostra, non ideo cogitandum est, ea ipsi non

displicent.
2. A quo fiat remissio peccatorum.
REmissio peccatorum fit a solo Deo, qui (ut inquit Pro-
pheta) delet iniquitates nostras: & quidem a Patre,
Filio, & S.S. Nam in trium nomen baptizamur. Baptis-
mus autem, ut & de Ioannis Baptismo dicitur, fit in re-
missionem peccatorum: ac de Filio manifeste dicit Scrip-
tura: Filium hominis habere potestatem remittendi peccata.
Similiter de S. sancto dicitur, quod tentatus fuerit: quod
offendatur & contristetur. Proinde & ipse peccata potest
remittere. Nullus enim peccata remittere potest, nisi
in quem peccatur, & qui in peccatis offenditur. Ac di-
sertis etiam verbis de peccato in S. sanctum Christus
apud Euangelistas loquitur. Causa autem quod a solo deo,
a solo nempe Patre, Filio, & S.S. peccata remittantur, haec
est, quia nemo nisi pars offensa potest remittere peccata: at so-

page.notes: Marginal references in the left margin were placed beside the lines they stand against; the reference "A&.5.9." is printed with the ampersand ligature for "ct" and is kept as printed. Long s throughout is read as s. The final mark after the text ("O") is uncertain; it is given as a signature with [?]. The drop cap R of "Remissio" is joined to the word. The word after "Ac di-" is read as "disertis" (long s as printed), with the hyphen kept as printed. Some italic/roman boundaries in the phrases "Causa autem quod a solo deo" and "quia nemo nisi pars offensa" are reconstructed from the typeface and may be imprecise.
